precepts.text: The days come that I will bring again the captivity of my people Israel and Judah, and I will cause them to return to the land that I gave to their fathers, and they shall possess it. We went over this last week. Now we know what Joel 3:1 is saying.
precepts.point: In those days, and in that time, when I shall bring again the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem: meaning he is going to bring us back to our homeland. Here is the evidence.
precepts.why:
Joel opens with “in those days, and in that time, when I shall bring again the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem”. Jeremiah shows what that means: “For, lo, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will bring again the captivity of my people Israel and Judah, saith the Lord: and I will cause them to return to the land that I gave to their fathers, and they shall possess it.”

To bring again the captivity is to bring us back to our homeland, the land given to our fathers, and to possess it. That is the evidence. Now we know what Joel 3:1 is saying.

And it ties the whole chapter together. The Most High gathers all nations into the valley of Jehoshaphat, in Israel, at the place called Har-Megiddo, where the name Armageddon comes from, to plead with them for his people and his heritage Israel, whom they scattered among the nations while they parted his land between the Arabs and the Edomites.

Joel ends the same way it begins: “Behold, I will raise them out of the place whither ye have sold them”. The Most High raises up the Israelites out of the places they were sold into, back to verse 1, and brings us home to our land in freedom.

precepts.text: All that devour thee shall be devoured and all thine adversaries go into captivity; every nation had a hand in spoiling us, the Arabs included, and what you see overseas is the Lord's righteous judgment.
precepts.point: For a prey and none delivereth, for a spoil and none saith restore: no nation speaks on our behalf unless a cheque is involved, and none will restore what it stole, from Henrietta Lacks' cells on down, because restoring us means giving back everything.
precepts.why:
Isaiah calls Israel “a people robbed and spoiled.” We are robbed of our nationality, robbed of the understanding that we are the twelve tribes of the children of Israel. Jeremiah shows how we are spoiled, and what the Lord will do about it.

“Therefore all they that devour thee shall be devoured”: that is going to take place upon the oppressors of our people. “and all thine adversaries, every one of them, shall go into captivity”: the adversaries are all the nations outside of the children of Israel, and every one of the nations that oppress us shall go into captivity.

How do they spoil us? Over a multitude of captivities the children of Israel have gone into, every single nation has had its hand in the oppression of the twelve tribes. That includes the Arabs, that a lot of brothers and sisters want to cry over when they see what is going on in Palestine. Those people had our people oppressed too; they were spoiling the hell out of us. What we are seeing overseas right now is the righteous judgment of the Lord, prophecy fulfilling right now.

Yet brothers and sisters are so damn fearful to escape this captivity and get themselves together, even as the prophecies come to pass. Many are called, but few are chosen, so self-examine. With bombs dropping and rumors of war, men are still catting around, committing fornication, letting their wives rule over them and hide their folly, paying for prostitutes, hooked on marijuana and controlled by the porn system. Our people are sick; they are afraid of freedom, because sin controls them.

“and they that spoil thee shall be a spoil, and all that prey upon thee will I give for a prey.” The nations that spoiled us shall in turn be a spoil for us, because the tables are turned. We serve a just God. So Isaiah’s people “for a prey” and “for a spoil” will not stay that way: those that prey upon Israel are given for a prey themselves.

precepts.text: When I shall bring again the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem: the same words, and Jeremiah explains them as a return from captivity.
precepts.point: Alas, for that day is great, so that none is like it; it is the time of Jacob's trouble, but he shall be saved out of it.
precepts.why:
“Write thee all the words that I have spoken unto thee in a book.” That book is called the Bible today. Then pay attention: “For, lo, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will bring again the captivity of my people Israel and Judah”.

Joel 3:1 confuses some brothers: “For, behold, in those days, and in that time, when I shall bring again the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem”. Read that alone and you think it means he is bringing us back into slavery. That is not what it means.

Go back to Jeremiah 30:3. Notice the same words, except Jeremiah explains them: “and I will cause them to return to the land that I gave to their fathers, and they shall possess it.” When he says he will bring again the captivity, he is speaking of bringing us back from captivity, not into captivity. Jeremiah explains Joel.

precepts.text: Oh that I had in the wilderness a lodging place, that I might leave my people, for they are all adulterers who bend their tongues for lies and are not valiant for the truth: valiant in the theatre for Nat Turner and Malcolm, but not on the earth.
precepts.point: Alas, for that day is great, so that none is like it; it is the time of Jacob's trouble, but he shall be saved out of it.
precepts.why:
“We have heard a voice of trembling, of fear, and not of peace.” We are coming up on that moment now. And yet our people cheer the movies on Martin Luther King and Malcolm X. You may not agree with Martin's method, but how many of us would walk down the street knowing we would be beaten, jailed and have dogs sicced on us? Their stand ended Jim Crow, and in sixty years of that liberty, how have we used it? We shoot each other, besmirch one another and hate each other.

Jeremiah said, “Oh that I had in the wilderness a lodging place of wayfaring men; that I might leave my people, and go from them!” He wanted to leave black people. Why? “for they be all adulterers, an assembly of treacherous men. And they bend their tongues like their bow for lies”. Black people love to use their lips for lies.

“but they are not valiant for the truth upon the earth”. They are valiant in the movie theatre. They cheer on Nat Turner in Birth of a Nation, cheer on Malcolm X and Martin Luther King, cheer the resistance in The Hunger Games and Star Wars, but they do not have that spirit and do not have the balls to do what those men did. They would never have joined Malcolm or Martin, and many will not join us out of fear. Two young boys got shot in the face in Georgia, instigated by a gaggle of other black men who scattered like cockroaches and played innocent when the cops came. So-called revolutionary brothers on podcasts call us a cult while including homosexuality and transgenderism; they have never left the couch.

“for they proceed from evil to evil, and they know not me, saith the Lord.” That is why, in the time of Jacob's trouble, there is a voice of trembling and fear and not of peace.

precepts.text: Israel abides many days without a king, a prince or a sacrifice; afterward they return and seek the Lord their God and David their king.
precepts.point: Fear thou not, O my servant Jacob: what he says will happen makes us afraid, so we increase our faith by remembering this body is a shell. I will save thee from afar and thy seed from the land of their captivity, and Jacob shall return and be in rest and none shall make him afraid. Though I make a full end of all nations, the extras born in vain with Esau the villain, I will not make a full end of thee, but correct thee in measure and not leave thee altogether unpunished.
precepts.why:
“In that day”, “I will break his yoke from off thy neck, and will burst thy bonds, and strangers shall no more serve themselves of him”: that's Christ's return. “But they shall serve the Lord their God, and David their king, whom I will raise up unto them.” Uh-oh. Did you notice? David is alive.

Hosea says the same: “For the children of Israel shall abide many days without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an image, and without an ephod, and without teraphim”. Many days without a king. “Afterward shall the children of Israel return, and seek the Lord their God, and David their king; and shall fear the Lord and his goodness in the latter days.”

We are returning now. We are seeking the Lord our God. And it is telling you David is going to be alive in these last days, in the latter days, when Israel returns. That is the day of Jeremiah 30, when the yoke is broken off our neck and the Lord raises David up unto us.

precepts.text: There is no remembrance of former things: David will not remember who he is, and neither do you.
precepts.point: Fear thou not, O my servant Jacob: what he says will happen makes us afraid, so we increase our faith by remembering this body is a shell. I will save thee from afar and thy seed from the land of their captivity, and Jacob shall return and be in rest and none shall make him afraid. Though I make a full end of all nations, the extras born in vain with Esau the villain, I will not make a full end of thee, but correct thee in measure and not leave thee altogether unpunished.
precepts.why:
If David is alive in these last days, “David their king, whom I will raise up unto them”, why doesn't anyone know it? Solomon says: “There is no remembrance of former things; neither shall there be any remembrance of things that are to come with those that shall come after.”

David will not remember who he is, and neither do you. Our minds are wiped, everybody. We don't know who's who. That is why it says love your neighbour as you love yourself: you don't know who is who.

And that is a good thing. In the old school we used to say, oh, this one's David, and that caused a lot of partiality and a lot of problems. Don't do that. Don't try to guess who anybody is either. Little brother calling himself Samson: you don't know, brother. Just stop it. The Lord will raise up David; it is not ours to name him.

precepts.text: I will set up one shepherd over them, my servant David, and he shall feed them.
precepts.point: Fear thou not, O my servant Jacob: what he says will happen makes us afraid, so we increase our faith by remembering this body is a shell. I will save thee from afar and thy seed from the land of their captivity, and Jacob shall return and be in rest and none shall make him afraid. Though I make a full end of all nations, the extras born in vain with Esau the villain, I will not make a full end of thee, but correct thee in measure and not leave thee altogether unpunished.
precepts.why:
Jeremiah says Israel “shall serve the Lord their God, and David their king, whom I will raise up unto them.” Ezekiel says the same of the last days: “And I will set up one shepherd over them, and he shall feed them, even my servant David; he shall feed them, and he shall be their shepherd.”

One shepherd over the whole nation, and that shepherd is David. After Israel has abided many days without a king, the Lord himself sets David up over them, to feed them.

That is part of the promise that comes at the end of the exile and tribulation: the yoke broken from our neck, the strangers no longer serving themselves of us, Jacob returned to rest and quiet with none to make him afraid, and one shepherd, David, raised up over Israel under the Lord their God.

precepts.text: Let the multitude perish which was born in vain: the nations are the extras in the movie, and we are the stars.
precepts.point: Fear thou not, O my servant Jacob: what he says will happen makes us afraid, so we increase our faith by remembering this body is a shell. I will save thee from afar and thy seed from the land of their captivity, and Jacob shall return and be in rest and none shall make him afraid. Though I make a full end of all nations, the extras born in vain with Esau the villain, I will not make a full end of thee, but correct thee in measure and not leave thee altogether unpunished.
precepts.why:
“though I make a full end of all nations whither I have scattered thee, yet will I not make a full end of thee”. Why is he going to make an end of all nations? Ezra says it: “Let the multitude perish then, which was born in vain”.

All these nations were born in vain. In a movie they are the extras; they're not the stars of the movie. We are. And Esau is the villain, the antagonist, the bad guy.

But the stars are not spared from correction: “I will correct thee in measure, and will not leave thee altogether unpunished.” The Lord makes a full end of the nations, but only corrects Israel in measure. So “fear thou not, O my servant Jacob”. What he says will happen would make anyone afraid, and nobody wants to go through tribulation, so we increase our faith by reminding ourselves that this body is just a shell; the real us is within. He will save us from afar, and Jacob shall return and be in rest, and none shall make him afraid.

precepts.text: Ah sinful nation, a seed of evildoers who revolt more and more; the whole head is sick and there is no soundness from the foot to the head, wounds not mollified with ointment: no healing but the Saviour.
precepts.point: Therefore all they that devour thee shall be devoured and all thine adversaries, every one of them, shall go into captivity, Miss Laura included, and all that prey upon thee shall be a prey. For I will restore health unto thee: only the Lord heals, by Christ's stripes, for they that are whole need no physician and he came to call sinners to repentance. Because they call thee an outcast, African-American, Haitian, Jamaican, this is Zion whom no man seeketh after.
precepts.why:
“Thy bruise is incurable, and thy wound is grievous. There is none to plead thy cause, that thou mayest be bound up: thou hast no healing medicines.” None stands up on our behalf, and we have no healing medicine. Every Negro that just popped out of his mama's behind has a new idea for how to save black people, and it is always economics or voting. Those medicines don't work. What is the wound? Our sins. Isaiah says the same thing.

“Ah sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a seed of evildoers, children that are corrupters: they have forsaken the Lord, they have provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger, they are gone away backward.” We are that sinful nation, a people laden with sin; iniquity is sin. He calls us a seed of evildoers.

“Why should ye be stricken any more? ye will revolt more and more”. Our people get punished and revolt more and more against God. Then: “the whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint”: the whole head of the Israelites is sick.

“From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it; but wounds, and bruises, and putrifying sores: they have not been closed, neither bound up, neither mollified with ointment.” Neither mollified with ointment means no medicine: there is no healing for us that way. That is Jeremiah's “no healing medicines.”

The only one who can save us is the Saviour, Jesus Christ, our master, our king. Yes, he is our rabbi, and rabbi means master. The wound Jeremiah calls incurable is incurable by any remedy of men; only the Lord can say, “I will restore health unto thee”.

precepts.text: Satan smote Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown: what Isaiah says of the nation is what Job went through, and Job was blessed at the end.
precepts.point: Therefore all they that devour thee shall be devoured and all thine adversaries, every one of them, shall go into captivity, Miss Laura included, and all that prey upon thee shall be a prey. For I will restore health unto thee: only the Lord heals, by Christ's stripes, for they that are whole need no physician and he came to call sinners to repentance. Because they call thee an outcast, African-American, Haitian, Jamaican, this is Zion whom no man seeketh after.
precepts.why:
What Isaiah and Jeremiah say of the nation is the same thing Job went through. People read Job and think that was only him, but Job's real life symbolizes the nation of Israel. This was the fifth judgment on Job: “So went Satan forth from the presence of the Lord, and smote Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown.” Didn't we just read that in Isaiah 1? “From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it”.

Job's life is Deuteronomy 28. He lost his businesses, his family, everything. And “There is none to plead thy cause”: Job had friends who would not stand up on his behalf. They were always telling him he was wrong, evil, the devil. There was no cure; God had to intervene and heal Job. That is why the Lord sent Christ to heal the twelve tribes of Israel.

Even Job's wife turned on him in his darkest moment, when he had lost everything. That is how these black women do with us: in this state, the black woman turned on us.

But at the end of Job's life he was blessed. That is what is going to happen to us if we endure to the end: the incurable wound of Jeremiah 30 ends with “I will restore health unto thee, and I will heal thee of thy wounds”.

precepts.text: God walked contrary unto them and brought them into the land of their enemies; if their uncircumcised hearts be humbled and they accept of the punishment of their iniquity: we have to accept that God was right and we were wrong, as a parent beats a child out of the street.
precepts.point: Therefore all they that devour thee shall be devoured and all thine adversaries, every one of them, shall go into captivity, Miss Laura included, and all that prey upon thee shall be a prey. For I will restore health unto thee: only the Lord heals, by Christ's stripes, for they that are whole need no physician and he came to call sinners to repentance. Because they call thee an outcast, African-American, Haitian, Jamaican, this is Zion whom no man seeketh after.
precepts.why:
“I have wounded thee with the wound of an enemy, with the chastisement of a cruel one, for the multitude of thine iniquity; because thy sins were increased.” Our sins are increased: the Houston rodeo, black men and women whoring themselves out, filthy and wicked, so bad a dress code had to be put in place; and in Delta State in Nigeria, a festival where women are openly raped in the streets. That is evil. Then: “because thy sins were increased, I have done these things unto thee”.

Moses said it would be so: “And that I also have walked contrary unto them, and have brought them into the land of their enemies”. God walked contrary to us because we kept breaking his laws, and he brought us into the land of our enemies. Then what we must do: “if then their uncircumcised hearts be humbled, and they then accept of the punishment of their iniquity”.

As we repent, we have to accept that God is right and we are wrong. We have always been wrong. God was just when he punished us. When your child plays in the street or with the light socket, you beat that behind, not because you hate him but so he learns he'll die playing in traffic or with electricity. Some talking doesn't do any good for some kids; you have to rile up on them so they know it's serious. That is what God did with us.

The three holy children did exactly this. In the midst of the fiery furnace, cast in because they would not worship Babylon's god, Azarias prayed: “Blessed art thou, O Lord God of our fathers”, “For thou art righteous in all the things that thou hast done to us: yea, true are all thy works, thy ways are right, and all thy judgments truth.” Then: “for according to truth and judgment didst thou bring all these things upon us because of our sins. For we have sinned and committed iniquity, departing from thee”. Everything God has done to our people is justified, because we revolted against him. They said it because of what Moses said in Leviticus, and what happened to them is a reflection of what will happen to us.

Christianity has taught our people the opposite: to mock a God who got angry at his own people for worshipping a golden calf. But accepting the punishment is the way back, because the next verse is: “Then will I remember my covenant with Jacob”.

precepts.text: He spake of the kingdom of God and healed them that had need of healing: Christ is the only one who can heal us.
precepts.point: Therefore all they that devour thee shall be devoured and all thine adversaries, every one of them, shall go into captivity, Miss Laura included, and all that prey upon thee shall be a prey. For I will restore health unto thee: only the Lord heals, by Christ's stripes, for they that are whole need no physician and he came to call sinners to repentance. Because they call thee an outcast, African-American, Haitian, Jamaican, this is Zion whom no man seeketh after.
precepts.why:
“For I will restore health unto thee, and I will heal thee of thy wounds, saith the Lord”. The Lord is the only one who can restore health; that goes back to verses 12 and 13, “thou hast no healing medicines.” There is no magic voting right and no economic situation to save us.

Luke shows who the healer is: “And the people, when they knew it, followed him: and he received them, and spake unto them of the kingdom of God, and healed them that had need of healing.” Christ spake of the kingdom and healed them that had need of healing. He is the only one who can heal us of all these things. He is the Saviour; he is the physician.

That is how the incurable bruise of Jeremiah 30 is cured. Not by any medicine of man, but by the Lord who received the people, taught them the kingdom of God, and healed them.

precepts.text: They that are whole have no need of the physician; I came not to call the righteous but sinners to repentance.
precepts.point: Therefore all they that devour thee shall be devoured and all thine adversaries, every one of them, shall go into captivity, Miss Laura included, and all that prey upon thee shall be a prey. For I will restore health unto thee: only the Lord heals, by Christ's stripes, for they that are whole need no physician and he came to call sinners to repentance. Because they call thee an outcast, African-American, Haitian, Jamaican, this is Zion whom no man seeketh after.
precepts.why:
Christ is the physician: “When Jesus heard it, he saith unto them, They that are whole have no need of the physician, but they that are sick”. If you think you're good, that you know everything, you don't need the son of God, you don't need the Saviour.

You have to admit you're sick: that we are in the midst of sin, and that all we have done has been wrong. That is the same thing as accepting the punishment of our iniquity.

“I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.” He did not call us righteous. He came for sinners. That is the healing Jeremiah promises Israel, whose “sorrow is incurable for the multitude of thine iniquity”. The sick nation is the one he came to heal.

The churches are the opposite: they say they don't need that Bible, they are already whole. Isaiah 65 shows them saying so, “I am holier than thou.” The ones who think themselves whole will not come to the physician.

precepts.text: Found of them that sought me not, a nation not called by my name; a rebellious people walking after their own thoughts in Christianity and Islam, sacrificing in gardens, eating swine's flesh and broth of abominable things, and saying stand by thyself, I am holier than thou, washed in the blood: a smoke in his nose.
precepts.point: Therefore all they that devour thee shall be devoured and all thine adversaries, every one of them, shall go into captivity, Miss Laura included, and all that prey upon thee shall be a prey. For I will restore health unto thee: only the Lord heals, by Christ's stripes, for they that are whole need no physician and he came to call sinners to repentance. Because they call thee an outcast, African-American, Haitian, Jamaican, this is Zion whom no man seeketh after.
precepts.why:
This goes with Christ saying he came not for the righteous but for sinners. “I am sought of them that asked not for me; I am found of them that sought me not”. Like the disciples, we didn't wake up one day as kids searching for the Lord of heaven and earth. The word was introduced to us and woke us up.

“I said, Behold me, behold me, unto a nation that was not called by my name.” We are called African-Americans, Haitians, Jamaicans, Puerto Ricans. That is a nation not called by his name.

“I have spread out my hands all the day unto a rebellious people, which walketh in a way that was not good, after their own thoughts”. We are that rebellious people, walking in Christianity and Islam, our people following their own thoughts in these religions. “A people that provoketh me to anger continually to my face; that sacrificeth in gardens, and burneth incense upon altars of brick”: the churches and mosques. Then: “which eat swine’s flesh, and broth of abominable things is in their vessels”. You know that's the church: there was always a swine fest at the end, pig feet and all of that; possum soup, turtle soup.

“Which say, Stand by thyself, come not near to me; for I am holier than thou.” That is what the churches say to the Israelites on the street preaching: stand by yourself, I don't need no black Jesus, I'm washed in the blood of Jesus, I'm water baptized, I'm holier than thou. “These are a smoke in my nose, a fire that burneth all the day.” God can't stand them.

That is the people Jeremiah calls an Outcast, “This is Zion, whom no man seeketh after.” Those who think they are whole push away the physician; the sick who admit it are the ones he heals.

precepts.text: Who his own self bare our sins in his own body on the tree, by whose stripes ye were healed: how the Lord restores health.
precepts.point: Therefore all they that devour thee shall be devoured and all thine adversaries, every one of them, shall go into captivity, Miss Laura included, and all that prey upon thee shall be a prey. For I will restore health unto thee: only the Lord heals, by Christ's stripes, for they that are whole need no physician and he came to call sinners to repentance. Because they call thee an outcast, African-American, Haitian, Jamaican, this is Zion whom no man seeketh after.
precepts.why:
How does the Lord restore health unto us? “Who his own self bare our sins in his own body on the tree, that we, being dead to sins, should live unto righteousness: by whose stripes ye were healed.”

Christ bare our sins in his own body on the tree, which is the cross; the cross was made from a tree. We, being dead to sin, should live unto righteousness. We are healed by Christ's punishment, his crucifixion.

That is the prophecy of Jeremiah 30:17: “For I will restore health unto thee, and I will heal thee of thy wounds, saith the Lord”. How? When he sent Christ to die on the cross. By his stripes we are healed.

Then: “because they called thee an Outcast, saying, This is Zion, whom no man seeketh after”. Outcast means African-American: made-up names they gave our race. Nobody gives a damn about you, blacks and Latinos; no man seeks after you. But the Lord does. The wound no medicine could close is healed by his stripes, and then “all they that devour thee shall be devoured; and all thine adversaries, every one of them, shall go into captivity”: every one of them, not some.

precepts.text: The children of Israel pitch their tents every man by his own camp and his own standard: Judah with Judah, Ephraim with Ephraim.
precepts.point: The whirlwind of the Lord goeth forth with fury and falls upon the head of the wicked, and the fierce anger of the Lord shall not return until he hath performed the intents of his heart; in the latter days ye shall consider it.
precepts.why:
Just before this, the Lord says, “I will restore health unto thee, and I will heal thee of thy wounds”, and that healing came when he sent Christ to die on the cross: by his stripes we are healed. “because they called thee an Outcast”: outcast means African-American, made-up names for our race, a Zion “whom no man seeketh after”. Nobody gives a damn about blacks and Latinos. Then: “Behold, I will bring again the captivity of Jacob’s tents”.

What are Jacob’s tents? “And the children of Israel shall pitch their tents, every man by his own camp, and every man by his own standard, throughout their hosts.” Every man by his own camp: Judah is going to be with Judah, Ephraim with Ephraim, Benjamin with Benjamin. That is the restructuring, the restoration of a nation.

And every man by his own standard: Judah had the standard of the lion, Benjamin the wolf, Naphtali the deer, Ephraim the bull. When the Lord brings again the captivity of Jacob’s tents, all of this is being restored again: the tribes set back in order, each under its own standard.

precepts.text: How goodly are thy tents, O Jacob, and thy tabernacles, O Israel.
precepts.point: The whirlwind of the Lord goeth forth with fury and falls upon the head of the wicked, and the fierce anger of the Lord shall not return until he hath performed the intents of his heart; in the latter days ye shall consider it.
precepts.why:
All of this is being restored again: “How goodly are thy tents, O Jacob, and thy tabernacles, O Israel!”

The tents of Jacob, pitched every man by his own camp and his own standard, are goodly in the eyes of the Lord. These are the same tents Jeremiah speaks of when the Lord says, “I will bring again the captivity of Jacob’s tents, and have mercy on his dwellingplaces”.

So the promise of Jeremiah 30:18 is that the goodly order Israel had in the wilderness, the tribes camped in their tents, is brought back out of captivity. What was taken captive, the Lord returns, and Jacob’s tents are goodly again.

precepts.text: He cast out the heathen, divided them an inheritance by line and made the tribes of Israel to dwell in their tents.
precepts.point: The whirlwind of the Lord goeth forth with fury and falls upon the head of the wicked, and the fierce anger of the Lord shall not return until he hath performed the intents of his heart; in the latter days ye shall consider it.
precepts.why:
“He cast out the heathen also before them, and divided them an inheritance by line, and made the tribes of Israel to dwell in their tents.” He cast out the heathen before us, divided the land to the tribes by line, and set each tribe in its tents.

That is what it means for the Lord to bring again the captivity of Jacob’s tents. The tents of Jacob are the tribes of Israel dwelling in their own inheritance, and to bring them again is to cast out the heathen once more and set the twelve tribes back in their inheritance.

Then Jeremiah goes on: “and the city shall be builded upon her own heap”, because that land is going to be destroyed and built again, and the tribes dwell in it again as the Lord made them to dwell at the first.

precepts.text: The sons of strangers build thy walls and their kings minister unto thee, and the glory of Lebanon beautifies the place of my sanctuary: the palace built on her own heap.
precepts.point: The whirlwind of the Lord goeth forth with fury and falls upon the head of the wicked, and the fierce anger of the Lord shall not return until he hath performed the intents of his heart; in the latter days ye shall consider it.
precepts.why:
“the city shall be builded upon her own heap, and the palace shall remain after the manner thereof.” It says heap because that land is going to be destroyed and built again; the palace means the temple that is going to be built. Isaiah 60 goes with Jeremiah 30:18.

“And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls, and their kings shall minister unto thee: for in my wrath I smote thee, but in my favour have I had mercy on thee.” The strangers build the walls when Jerusalem is built again on her own heap.

“The glory of Lebanon shall come unto thee, the fir tree, the pine tree, and the box together, to beautify the place of my sanctuary”. That is the palace. “and I will make the place of my feet glorious”: the Lord is going to make Jerusalem glorious again.

precepts.text: Thy people shall be all righteous and inherit the land for ever, and a little one shall become a thousand and a small one a strong nation.
precepts.point: The whirlwind of the Lord goeth forth with fury and falls upon the head of the wicked, and the fierce anger of the Lord shall not return until he hath performed the intents of his heart; in the latter days ye shall consider it.
precepts.why:
Jeremiah says, “I will multiply them, and they shall not be few; I will also glorify them, and they shall not be small.” That is why we go to Isaiah 60.

“Thy people also shall be all righteous: they shall inherit the land for ever, the branch of my planting, the work of my hands, that I may be glorified.” Then: “A little one shall become a thousand, and a small one a strong nation: I the Lord will hasten it in his time.” We shall not be small.

There is more in that verse than what it is saying on the surface. Look at the little bodies we have now. We are not going to have these little bodies. We are not going to be all frail and skinny, and the little fat brothers are not going to be like that either. The Lord multiplies and glorifies Israel, in number and in body.

precepts.text: I will purge away thy dross and restore thy judges as at the first: everything returned to our glorious state.
precepts.point: The whirlwind of the Lord goeth forth with fury and falls upon the head of the wicked, and the fierce anger of the Lord shall not return until he hath performed the intents of his heart; in the latter days ye shall consider it.
precepts.why:
“Their children also shall be as aforetime, and their congregation shall be established before me”. The Lord is going to return it all back to the way it was.

Isaiah says the same: “And I will turn my hand upon thee, and purely purge away thy dross, and take away all thy tin:” “And I will restore thy judges as at the first”. He purges the dross out of Israel and restores the judges as at the first, the way it was in the beginning.

That is what Jeremiah 30:20 is saying: our children as aforetime, our congregation established before the Lord, everything returned to our glorious state. And it answers verse 21 too, “their nobles shall be of themselves”: our own judges, restored as at the first.

precepts.text: The Lord saves the tents of Judah first; he that is feeble shall be as David, and the house of David, the 144,000, as God, as the angel of the Lord before them.
precepts.point: The whirlwind of the Lord goeth forth with fury and falls upon the head of the wicked, and the fierce anger of the Lord shall not return until he hath performed the intents of his heart; in the latter days ye shall consider it.
precepts.why:
“The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first, that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem do not magnify themselves against Judah.” These are the same tents of Jacob that the Lord brings again out of captivity.

“In that day shall the Lord defend the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and he that is feeble among them at that day shall be as David”. The feeble Israelites are going to be like King David. “and the house of David shall be as God, as the angel of the Lord before them.” The house of David is the 144,000; they shall be as God.

That is our children being as aforetime and our glorious state being restored: the Lord saving Judah’s tents first, and the weakest of Israel made as strong as David.

precepts.text: He shall judge the poor, save the children of the needy and break in pieces the oppressor: no coming together with him.
precepts.point: The whirlwind of the Lord goeth forth with fury and falls upon the head of the wicked, and the fierce anger of the Lord shall not return until he hath performed the intents of his heart; in the latter days ye shall consider it.
precepts.why:
At the bottom of Jeremiah 30:20 the Lord says, “I will punish all that oppress them.” He said all, not some. All that have oppressed us shall be punished.

The precept is Psalms 72: “He shall judge the poor of the people, he shall save the children of the needy, and shall break in pieces the oppressor.” Break in pieces the oppressor.

There is no coming together and joining with the oppressor. The Lord did not say he would reconcile Israel with the ones who oppressed them; he said, I am going to break them. That is the punishment of all that oppress us.

precepts.text: Out of Bethlehem in the land of Judah shall come a governor that shall rule my people Israel: Christ, our governor from the midst of us.
precepts.point: The whirlwind of the Lord goeth forth with fury and falls upon the head of the wicked, and the fierce anger of the Lord shall not return until he hath performed the intents of his heart; in the latter days ye shall consider it.
precepts.why:
“And their nobles shall be of themselves, and their governor shall proceed from the midst of them”. Our nobles are going to come from our own people. We are not going to have nobles of another race, like the mayor they have now in New York, Mamdani. That is not our people.

Christ is our governor, and he came from the midst of us: “And thou Bethlehem, in the land of Juda, art not the least among the princes of Juda: for out of thee shall come a Governor, that shall rule my people Israel.” That is Christ right there.

So the governor that proceeds from the midst of Israel is Christ, born in Bethlehem of Judah, ruling his people Israel. “I will cause him to draw near, and he shall approach unto me”, and then, “ye shall be my people, and I will be your God.”

precepts.text: In those days and in that time, when I shall bring again the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem. The same phrase as Jeremiah 30, the return to the land.
precepts.point: Alas, for that day is great, so that none is like it; it is even the time of Jacob's trouble, but he shall be saved out of it. That is the great tribulation.
precepts.why:
The Lord told Jeremiah, “Write thee all the words that I have spoken unto thee in a book”: the Bible. “For, lo, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will bring again the captivity of my people Israel and Judah”.

Joel uses the same words: “For, behold, in those days, and in that time, when I shall bring again the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem”. Sometimes in your thoughts you might be saying that means the Lord is going to make us slaves again. No, that is not what it means.

Jeremiah explains it in the same verse: “and I will cause them to return to the land that I gave to their fathers, and they shall possess it.” To bring again the captivity is to bring us again to our land. That is the evidence. The same phrase in Joel 3:1 speaks of that same return of Judah and Jerusalem, in those days and in that time, the days of Jacob's trouble, out of which he shall be saved.

precepts.text: Ye shall be hated of all men for my name's sake, but he that endureth to the end shall be saved. They hate us because we are the sons and daughters of God. When they persecute you in this city, flee into another: check the real estate, citizenship, and residency when you travel, because one city may pop off and the next may not. Ye shall not have gone over the cities of Israel till the Son of man be come; we will not reach every Israelite.
precepts.point: Alas, for that day is great, so that none is like it; it is even the time of Jacob's trouble, but he shall be saved out of it. That is the great tribulation.
precepts.why:
“Alas! for that day is great, so that none is like it: it is even the time of Jacob’s trouble; but he shall be saved out of it.” That is the great tribulation. Jeremiah does not go into much detail on how he is saved out of it, so Christ fills it in.

“And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved.” Christ prophesied we would be hated of all men for his sake, so we have to endure the hatred. Brothers and sisters on TikTok, YouTube and Instagram ask why the white man hates us so much. Because we are the sons and daughters of God, the people of Christ.

“But when they persecute you in this city, flee ye into another”. So when you brothers go to these other countries, check out the real estate, find out whether you can get citizenship or residency, question and research, because if something pops off here we have to be able to move. One city may pop off and the next city may not have the same persecution.

“for verily I say unto you, Ye shall not have gone over the cities of Israel, till the Son of man be come.” We will not have reached all the twelve tribes before Christ comes; we are not going to reach every Israelite. Christ says the same in Matthew 24: they shall deliver you up to be afflicted and kill you, many shall be offended and betray one another, but he that endures unto the end, either your death or Christ's return, shall be saved.

precepts.text: I will send those that escape of them, the 144,000, unto the nations, to Tarshish, Pul, Lud, Tubal, Javan, and the isles afar off that have not heard my fame, and they shall bring all your brethren for an offering out of all nations upon horses, chariots, litters, and mules to my holy mountain Jerusalem, and I will take of them for priests and Levites. The kingdom is already set up when this happens; Papua New Guinea alone has thousands of islands.
precepts.point: Alas, for that day is great, so that none is like it; it is even the time of Jacob's trouble, but he shall be saved out of it. That is the great tribulation.
precepts.why:
How do we know we will not reach all the Israelites everywhere before Christ comes? Isaiah shows the rest are gathered after: “And I will set a sign among them, and I will send those that escape of them unto the nations”. Those that escape are the 144,000.

They are sent “to Tarshish”, Spain, “Pul”, Libya, “and Lud”, Lydia, “that draw the bow, to Tubal”, Turkey, “and Javan”, Greece, “to the isles afar off”, like the Melanesian isles. When we went to Papua New Guinea and looked at the map, there are thousands of islands there. These are places “that have not heard my fame, neither have seen my glory”: they have not heard the gospel. “and they shall declare my glory among the Gentiles.” The 144,000 collect the Israelites that are in these other nations.

“And they shall bring all your brethren for an offering unto the Lord out of all nations upon horses, and in chariots, and in litters, and upon mules, and upon swift beasts, to my holy mountain Jerusalem”. The kingdom is already set up at this time, and the third temple is built.

“And I will also take of them for priests and for Levites, saith the Lord.” The brothers and sisters gathered from among those nations, the Lord will make those men priests and Levites. That is how Jacob is saved out of his trouble and all Israel is brought again to the land.

precepts.text: Jacob shall return, and shall be in rest, and be quiet, and none shall make him afraid; the future deliverance carries the same promise as this blessing.
precepts.point: That is also how you know the people in the land of Israel today are not the real Jews: this prophecy of rest is not fulfilled on them. When the Most High saves Israel from captivity it will be the same again, and none shall make him afraid.

note.label: Leviticus 26: The Blessings and the Curses

precepts.why:
The Most High would give peace in the land: no enemies able to come against Israel, no war in the land, no one making the people afraid. That was fulfilled in the days of king Solomon, when there was rest on every side.

Jeremiah carries the same promise forward to the future deliverance: “Therefore fear thou not, O my servant Jacob, saith the Lord; neither be dismayed, O Israel: for, lo, I will save thee from afar, and thy seed from the land of their captivity; and Jacob shall return, and shall be in rest, and be quiet, and none shall make him afraid.” The words are the words of the blessing in Leviticus.

That is also how you know the people in the land of Israel today are not the real Jews: this prophecy of rest is not fulfilled on them. When the Most High saves Israel from captivity it will be the same again, and none shall make him afraid.

precepts.text: A sinful nation laden with iniquity, the whole head sick and no soundness, wounds and bruises not closed nor bound up, because the sin has not been cut off.
precepts.point: Therefore all they that devour thee shall be devoured, the adversaries shall go into captivity, and they that spoil thee shall be a spoil; He will restore health and heal thy wounds because they called thee an outcast, Zion whom no man seeketh after, and He will put us back on high after the reproof.

note.label: Jeremiah 30: The Time of Jacob's Trouble

precepts.why:
Jeremiah says “Thy bruise is incurable, and thy wound is grievous”, with no healing medicines and none to plead thy cause. Isaiah shows the same body: “Ah sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a seed of evildoers, children that are corrupters: they have forsaken the Lord, they have provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger, they are gone away backward.”

“Why should ye be stricken any more? ye will revolt more and more: the whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint. From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it; but wounds, and bruises, and putrifying sores: they have not been closed, neither bound up, neither mollified with ointment.” The wound is incurable because the sin has not been cut off; the wounds are left open, not closed nor bound up.

The Lord wounded us with the wound of an enemy for the multitude of our iniquity, because our sins were increased. The healing is coming from the prophets with the word of God, the laws of God; that is what will heal us. Then he restores health, heals our wounds, and puts us back on high after the reproof, because they called us an outcast, Zion whom no man seeketh after.

precepts.text: All thy lovers have forgotten thee and seek thee not, for the Most High wounded thee with the wound of an enemy for the multitude of thine iniquity.
precepts.point: Israel's lovers and friends were other nations serving other gods, and when it got real they turned their backs, just as the Most High warned.

note.label: Lamentations 1: The City That Sits Solitary

precepts.why:
Jerusalem weeps and “among all her lovers she hath none to comfort her: all her friends have dealt treacherously with her, they are become her enemies.” Jeremiah had already said it: “All thy lovers have forgotten thee; they seek thee not; for I have wounded thee with the wound of an enemy, with the chastisement of a cruel one, for the multitude of thine iniquity; because thy sins were increased.”

Israel's lovers and friends were other nations serving other gods, and when it got real they turned their backs, just as the Most High warned. And it was he who wounded her, “with the wound of an enemy”, for the multitude of her iniquity. That is how the city that was full of people, great among the nations and princess among the provinces, came to sit solitary as a widow, with no one to comfort her.

points: Alas! for that day is great, so that none is like it: it is even the time of Jacob's trouble. Jacob's what? Trouble.
I am going to show you how we are a bunch of crazy handicapped people. Listen to this sister. If you think we are crazy —
This sister right there, she still does not see. She has no idea what is coming. You see that mindset? This is the mindset. I am telling you, God has to turn the heat on our people for us to change.

This week I made a video on Facebook. I was talking to our sisters. Let us talk about the welfare system for a minute. When you look at the welfare system, you got food stamps, you got Section 8, you got all these things, right? Some of our sisters thinking this system has to help me. The government wants to help us, that is why they created that system. That is not why they created that system.

I always said, when you look at a tree, do not look at the leaves of the tree. Look at the root of the tree. The tree did not start from the leaves. There is no tree that starts from top to bottom. It makes no sense. You got to look at the root. When you look at a problem, always look at the root. What caused the problem? The root of the problem.

note.label: Integrated but Divided: What Did We Lose?

points: Give me that Jeremiah real quick about Jacob's trouble. Because it is going to get worse than what it is right now.
Alas! for that day is great, so that none is like it: it is even the time of Jacob's trouble. It is what? It is even the time of Jacob's trouble.

That is what they are in right now in this movie I am showing you all. They are getting ready to go into Jacob's trouble. It is going to be hell and you need all hands on deck. That is why we pray for more labourers. That is why we are fasting and praying. That is why we had the prayer vigil. All these different things, because we understand the times that are ahead. Because our enemy, just like the white walkers, does not give a damn. All they see is blood. That is all they see. They do not care about nothing or nobody. They have shown you that time and time and time again.

But he shall be saved out of it. But he shall be saved out of it. Deliverance is coming. It is already written. We know where we are going to fall at. We are trying to make sure we get everybody else on board.
The clip continues: against their common enemy.

Pause. You see that? They fought together against the common enemy. The north and the south, black and Hispanic, fought together. That was during the sixties and seventies. We fought together during the times of the scriptures, when David ruled over one kingdom. They fought together.
The clip continues: despite their differences, despite their suspicions, together.
You see that? Despite the differences, they fought together. Why? Because their life was on the line. That is what we have got to understand. Some of you all do not get that.

The clip continues: we need to do the same if we are going to survive. Because the enemy is real. It has always been real. And you say you cannot defeat them without my armies and my dragons? No, I do not think I can. I will fight for you. I will fight for the north when you bend the knee.

All right, pause. So you see that she is still stuck on that same mindset. That is Christianity. It is like, yeah, what you all are saying is true, but this or that. It is like, you do not get it, man. It is bigger than this. It is bigger than your African Methodist Episcopal church. There is a white man out there that is hanging people. Do you all understand that? They are putting clone meat in the chicken. There are forty-eight ingredients to make a potato chip. What is that? You all have got to wake up and see what is going on.

Now I am going to show you all this in real life. Play the clip of Captain Mattathias when he is talking to the Christian pastor. This is the same situation Cap was in when he was out there dealing with the Christian pastors, just like Bishop did eight years ago when they were dealing with those other pastors.

The clip: I am just going to be honest here, I am known for speaking the truth. All of this is just a smoke screen because you all do not want to keep the law. You do not want to deal with the fact that Christ did not come for all nations. You all have not brought that up yet because you all want to draw this out, because you all know good and well that we have got to keep the commandments to inherit the kingdom of heaven. We know good and well that Christ did not come for all nations. He only came for the nation of Israel. We were told that today we will continue our conversation from part one. This had nothing to do with our conversation in part one. You are going to keep talking about if God cannot keep the covenant with Adam. You are not addressing who Christ came for. I am just being honest.
All right. So that is what we are dealing with. There are bigger issues at hand.

note.label: Unity: The Sweet Savor Of Salvation

points: We have heard a voice of trembling, of fear, and not of peace. Do not let anybody tell you that there will be peace on the earth. There will be no peace: it is death, destruction, and famine coming on this earth.
Wherefore do I see every man with his hands on his loins, as a woman in travail, and all faces are turned into paleness? Everybody holding their stomach; everybody scared.

Alas! for that day is great, so that none is like it: it is even the time of Jacob's trouble. Jacob's trouble is coming; great pains are coming. Brothers and sisters, prepare your mind; prepare yourself for what is coming. That is what the Lord commands us to do.

But brothers and sisters, the scripture has good news. For lo, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will bring again the captivity of my people Israel and Judah: both kingdoms, northern and southern.
And I will cause them to return to the land that I gave to their fathers, and they shall possess it. We shall possess the land.

note.label: Why They Hated US: Walking in the Footsteps of the Persecuted

points: For I am with thee, saith the Lord, to save thee: though I make a full end of all nations whither I have scattered thee, yet will I not make a full end of thee. That whole group we read in Psalms 83, every nation is ultimately going to be destroyed. Not the Israelites; we are going to be here. No other nation can claim that. We are in God's plans to be on this earth forever.

Us knowing this, all of this is temporary. The only way you would really go indulge in sin and in a bottle is because you do not believe. But if you believe, you will persevere through this. The Lord is not going to put more on us than we can handle; he said, I want you to make it, but I want to try you to make sure you are serious about keeping my commandments.

I will not make a full end of the righteous: some of our people are going to be destroyed, because they are going to choose the bottle, fornication, and debauchery over the Lord. But the ones that stay in righteousness will inherit the kingdom forever. If our brothers and sisters could endure slavery, we can endure this. And do not say, Lord, will I make it to the kingdom, that is up to you; that is a cop out. The Bible says give diligence to make your calling and election sure. That is on you.

But I will correct thee in measure: he is going to cause us to pass under the rod and teach us his commandments properly. We have some good days coming if we are steadfast. The way this system is set up is to make you believe you cannot escape it, to drive you into drugs, alcoholism, and evil; and if you succumb to that, you will be destroyed by it. The Lord said, fear not thou, O Jacob, for the Lord is our redeemer. We need to remember that.

note.label: The Developmental Psychology of Being Hated

points: Therefore all they that devour thee shall be devoured; and all thine adversaries, every one of them, shall go into captivity; and they that spoil thee shall be a spoil. You are where you are because you devoured the Israelites and used us for free labor.
So do not let anybody tell you that you are nothing right now. The Bible is your future; the Bible is your hope.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

points: Alas, for that day is great, so that none is like it; it is even the time of Jacob's trouble. Believe it or not, we have been talking about Jacob's trouble all day. Some of you think Jacob's trouble is just some hard times; no, Jacob's trouble comes with everything: the war, the famine, the betrayal. We are all going to go through it, brothers.

Write the words in a book: that is the Bible. I will bring again the captivity of my people Israel and Judah means bringing us back from captivity, not into it, because he says they shall return to the land and possess it; that clears up Joel 3:1.
A voice of trembling, of fear and not of peace: we are coming to that moment now. Every man with his hands on his loins as a woman in travail, and all faces turned into paleness.
Alas, for that day is great, so that none is like it; it is the time of Jacob's trouble, but he shall be saved out of it.

In that day I will break his yoke from off thy neck and burst thy bonds, and strangers shall no more serve themselves of him: Christ's return. They shall serve the Lord their God and David their king whom I will raise up: David is alive in the last days, and Israel returns after many days without a king to seek the Lord and David their king, and the Lord sets up one shepherd, my servant David.

There is no remembrance of former things, so David will not remember who he is and neither do we; do not guess who is who or call yourself Samson, because it causes partiality, and love your neighbour as yourself.

Fear thou not, O my servant Jacob: what he says will happen makes us afraid, so we increase our faith by remembering this body is a shell. I will save thee from afar and thy seed from the land of their captivity, and Jacob shall return and be in rest and none shall make him afraid. Though I make a full end of all nations, the extras born in vain with Esau the villain, I will not make a full end of thee, but correct thee in measure and not leave thee altogether unpunished.

Thy bruise is incurable and there is none to plead thy cause, thou hast no healing medicines: every Negro out of his mama has a new idea to save black people, economics or voting, and those medicines do not work, because the wound is our sins. Ah sinful nation, laden with iniquity, the whole head sick, wounds and putrefying sores not mollified with ointment: the only healer is the Saviour, our rabbi and master.

Job's life symbolises the nation: boils from the sole of his foot to his crown, friends who would not plead his cause, everything lost, and a wife who turned on him in his darkest moment, as the black woman does. God had to intervene, and at the end Job was blessed, as we will be if we endure.

All thy lovers have forgotten thee: the Chinese friends and the Arab friends, as Egypt and Ethiopia and Moab before, are gone. I have wounded thee for the multitude of thine iniquity because thy sins were increased, the Houston rodeo and the rape festival in Delta State, and God walked contrary to us and brought us into the land of our enemies; if our uncircumcised hearts be humbled and we accept the punishment of our iniquity, we admit God was right, as the three holy children sang in the furnace, thou art righteous in all the things thou hast done to us.

Therefore all they that devour thee shall be devoured and all thine adversaries, every one of them, shall go into captivity, Miss Laura included, and all that prey upon thee shall be a prey. For I will restore health unto thee: only the Lord heals, by Christ's stripes, for they that are whole need no physician and he came to call sinners to repentance. Because they call thee an outcast, African-American, Haitian, Jamaican, this is Zion whom no man seeketh after.

I will bring again the captivity of Jacob's tents: the children of Israel pitch their tents every man by his own camp and his own standard, Judah's lion and Benjamin's wolf, the restructuring of a nation; how goodly are thy tents, O Jacob, and he made the tribes to dwell in their tents.

The city shall be builded upon her own heap, because the land is destroyed and built again, and the palace, the temple, shall remain: the sons of strangers build thy walls, the glory of Lebanon beautifies the sanctuary, thy people shall be all righteous and inherit the land for ever, and a little one shall become a thousand, in bodies not frail or fat.

Out of them shall proceed thanksgiving and the voice of them that make merry, and I will multiply and glorify them. Their children shall be as aforetime, their congregation established before me, and I will punish all, not some, that oppress them; he shall break in pieces the oppressor, and there is no joining with him.

Their nobles shall be of themselves and their governor from the midst of them, not a Mamdani over New York: I will restore thy judges as at the first, the feeble shall be as David and the house of David, the 144,000, as God, and out of Bethlehem came a governor that shall rule my people Israel. Ye shall be my people and I will be your God.

The whirlwind of the Lord goeth forth with fury and falls upon the head of the wicked, and the fierce anger of the Lord shall not return until he hath performed the intents of his heart; in the latter days ye shall consider it.

Write all the words in a book, for the days come that I will bring again the captivity of my people Israel and Judah and cause them to return to the land I gave their fathers. Bringing again the captivity does not mean slavery again; verse 3 explains it as returning to the land, and Joel 3:1 says the same.

We have heard a voice of trembling, of fear, and not of peace. Ask whether a man travails with child: wherefore do I see every man with his hands on his loins as a woman in travail and all faces turned into paleness? Everybody is afraid.
Alas, for that day is great, so that none is like it; it is even the time of Jacob's trouble, but he shall be saved out of it. That is the great tribulation.

Though I make a full end of all nations whither I have scattered thee, yet will I not make a full end of thee, but I will correct thee in measure. Israel is in that correction now, and only Israel will remain.

note.label: Transforming From Immorality To Beautiful Civility Returning Our Kingdom To An Organized Nation Pt 3

points: The word came to Jeremiah to write all the words the Lord had spoken unto him in a book, showing that the Most High was dealing with Jeremiah and giving him his instructions unlike the other prophets.

note.label: Jeremiah 30: The Time of Jacob's Trouble

points: The days come that He will bring again the captivity of His people Israel and Judah, the northern and southern kingdom, and cause them to return to the land He gave to their fathers to possess it.

note.label: Jeremiah 30: The Time of Jacob's Trouble

points: These are the words concerning Israel and Judah: a voice of trembling, of fear and not of peace, every man with his hands on his loins as a woman in travail, and all faces turned pale.

note.label: Jeremiah 30: The Time of Jacob's Trouble

points: That day is great, so that none is like it; it is the time of Jacob's trouble, but he shall be saved out of it; this goes to the last days, this is prophecy of the great tribulation out of which Israel is saved.

note.label: Jeremiah 30: The Time of Jacob's Trouble

points: In that day the Most High will break the yoke from off thy neck, burst the bonds, and strangers shall no more serve themselves of him, but they shall serve the Lord their God and David their king whom He will raise up; that is the way we get that rulership, serving the Lord and Christ.

note.label: Jeremiah 30: The Time of Jacob's Trouble

points: Fear thou not O Jacob, neither be dismayed, for He will save thee from afar and thy seed from the land of their captivity, and Jacob shall return and be in rest with none to make him afraid.

note.label: Jeremiah 30: The Time of Jacob's Trouble

points: Though He makes a full end of all the nations whither He scattered thee, He will not make a full end of thee, but correct thee in measure and not leave thee altogether unpunished; the punishment is for our good, He will not destroy us.

note.label: Jeremiah 30: The Time of Jacob's Trouble

points: Thy bruise is incurable and thy wound grievous, none to plead thy cause, no healing medicines, and all thy lovers have forgotten thee; the Most High wounded thee with the wound of an enemy for the multitude of thine iniquity because thy sins were increased.

note.label: Jeremiah 30: The Time of Jacob's Trouble

points: The healing is coming from the prophets with the word of God, the laws of God; that is what will heal us.

Therefore all they that devour thee shall be devoured, the adversaries shall go into captivity, and they that spoil thee shall be a spoil; He will restore health and heal thy wounds because they called thee an outcast, Zion whom no man seeketh after, and He will put us back on high after the reproof.

note.label: Jeremiah 30: The Time of Jacob's Trouble

points: The Most High will bring again the captivity of Jacob's tents; the city shall be built upon her own heap, the palace remain, and out of them shall proceed thanksgiving and the voice of them that make merry, and He will multiply them and they shall not be few.

note.label: Jeremiah 30: The Time of Jacob's Trouble

points: He will glorify them and their children shall be as aforetime, their congregation established before Him with the Lord in the midst; nobles shall be of themselves and their governor from the midst of them, so no other nation rules over us, we rule ourselves under Christ who sets the order of who rules.

note.label: Jeremiah 30: The Time of Jacob's Trouble

points: The whirlwind of the Lord goes forth with fury upon the head of the wicked, and His fierce anger shall not return until He has performed the intent of His heart; in the latter days ye shall consider it, for He comes against the wicked of the other nations and those of our own people who will not submit to the laws of God.

note.label: Jeremiah 30: The Time of Jacob's Trouble

points: “I will bring again the captivity of my people Israel and Judah”. Both northern kingdom and southern kingdom. “and I will cause them to return to the land that I gave to their fathers, and they shall possess it.” God is going to give both kingdoms back our land.
